_doc: GENERIC build/integration ladder + stamping — the THIRD axis. Same skeleton as profiler_registry / verification_registry. Routes HOW a candidate kernel is built+tested: as a standalone translation unit, or wired into a project it cannot compile without (the llama.cpp case). The execution mechanism for embedded modes already exists (embedded/embedded_eval.js + ADAPTER_CONTRACT.md); this component only DECIDES the mode and stamps build_fidelity + reversibility. build_fidelity is the analog of profiling confidence: isolated < project_native < production.

standalone._doc: kernel compiles as its own translation unit. cheapest, lowest fidelity (may miss template instantiations / dispatch wiring).

embedded_inplace._doc: patch the kernel in place; build via the project's own build system. real build, but mutates the source file (restored on exit).

embedded_dispatch._doc: register an env-gated variant into the dispatch table; build via project. closest to production; non-mutating (original source untouched).

registry_dispatch._doc: python kernel-class registered into a runtime dispatch table (e.g. vLLM can_implement + register_linear_kernel). no C++ source touched.

sol_execbench_solution.eval_mechanism: embedded/sol_execbench_eval.js (pack candidate -> solution.json -> sol-execbench CLI -> parse per-workload speedup_factor geomean)
sol_execbench_solution._doc: candidate kernel is packaged into a sol-execbench solution.json (sources[] + spec entry_point/binding) and evaluated by the sol-execbench CLI, which compiles internally against the task harness. Non-mutating, no project source touched.

preference._doc: For a kernel that CANNOT compile standalone, prefer the highest-fidelity reversible mode the host supports: embedded_dispatch (non-mutating, production) > embedded_inplace (project_native) > registry_dispatch. standalone is intentionally NOT in this ladder — a confirmed-non-standalone kernel silently falling back to a doomed single-TU compile is dishonest; if no embedded mode is host-supported, route to derive_adapter so the agent sets up the project build. For a kernel that CAN compile standalone, standalone is correct (no project coupling).
